shared_elements: upright freestanding stone monolith set in ground
low-relief carving covering the front face
horizontal band of repeated pattern crossing the surface
animal/creature imagery including elongated serpent-like forms
raised rectangular or disc-shaped panel element
justification: Both are weathered upright carved monoliths whose front faces are divided into stacked registers, each crossed by a horizontal band of repeating pattern and populated with profile figures and elongated serpentine forms, which is the most specific correspondence. They differ sharply in execution and content: A is a dense, fine, angular composition dominated by a single frontal human figure in elaborate costume surrounded by block-like glyphic panels, while B is sparse and bold, with a few large rounded animal reliefs on a broad T-shaped block and no human figure or script-like elements.
